summary: This bill directs the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to establish a grant program for eligible entities to plant qualifying trees in historically redlined areas and urban heat islands, with a focus on community involvement and minimizing resident displacement.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly authorizes the appropriation of $50,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2036 to establish and carry out a grant program for tree planting. This directly increases government spending.

The bill authorizes $50 million annually for FY2026–2036 (total $550 million) for a new HUD tree-planting grant program with no offsets or revenue provisions, thereby increasing spending and the deficit to fund the program. Deficit reduction is not a purpose of the bill, which centers on urban forestry and environmental grants; the spending authorization is a supporting element rather than the focus.
